IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE  FIR/ORDER) NO. 9611 of 2018  ==========================================================
 SUMAIRVIJAY CHANDRAVIJAY SINGH & ORS.
 Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 HARSHESH R KAKKAD(7813) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3  MR RC KAKKAD(389) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3  MR MAHESH K POOJARA(5879) for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR HARDIK MEHTA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1

 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI

ORAL ORDER 1. Heard learned Senior Advocate Mr.Asim Pandya with learned advocate Mr.Harshesh Kakkad for the petitioners, learned advocate Mr.Poojara for respondent no.2 and learned APP for respondent - State.

2. By way of this petition, under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioners have prayed for quashment of the FIR being C.R.No.I - 35 of 2017 registered with Mahila Police Station,
Jamnagar against the petitioners for the offences punishable under the sections 498(A), 323, 504,
506(2) and 114 of Indian Penal Code and under section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act qua the petitioners.

3. At the outset, learned Senior Advocate Mr.Pandya submitted that petitioner no.3 viz. - Lekharajya Lakshmidevi has passed and he has tendered death certificate which is taken on NEUTRAL Sumairvijay Chandravijay Singh vs State Of Gujarat on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56432333/
1 CITATION R/CR.MA/9611/2018 ORDER DATED: 26/09/2025 undefined record, it indicates that Lekharjya has expired on 07.12.2021.
Thus, present petition qua petitioner no.3 stands abated.

4. So far as petitioner no.1 viz. Sumairvijay Chandravijay Singh is concerned, learned Senior Advocate Mr.Pandya does not press the petition with liberty to file appropriate proceedings as charge-sheet is filed against petitioner no.1.
The petition stands disposed of as withdrawn qua petitioner no.1.

The petitioner no.1 is at liberty to file appropriate proceedings before the learned Trial Court available under law and same shall be decided in accordance with law by the Court concerned without being influenced by withdrawal of present petition.

5. Before adverting to facts of the case as well as role of petitioner no.2 viz. Ahalyadevi @ Umabaa Chandravijay Singh in alleged offence, it is trite to observe that Transfer Petition No.30 of 2023 has filed by Pritika Singh before Hon'ble Apex Court to transfer Criminal Case No.6647 of 2017 pending in the Court of learned 7th Additional Senior Civil Judge, Jamnagar to Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, Indore, Madhya Pradesh.

The petition was allowed and accordingly, Criminal Case No.6647 of 2017 pending in the Court of learned ACJM, Jamnagar is transferred to Court of learned JMFC, Dr.Ambedkar Nagar, Indore, Madhya Pradesh.
Learned Advocate Mr.Poojara places on record order 22.10.2014 which indicates that case has been transferred as per order of Hon'ble Apex Court.

6. Another petition was filed before the Hon'ble Apex Court being Transfer Petition No.253 of 2025 whereby petitioner no.2 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9611/2018 ORDER DATED: 26/09/2025 undefined sought transfer of present petition from this Court to High Court of Madhya Pradesh.
Hon'ble Apex Court declined to entertain such petition.
In view of this, this Court continues to hold jurisdiction to address the issue as FIR in question is originally filed in the State of Gujarat.
7. Seeking quashment of questioned FIR, learned advocate for the petitioners submits that petitioner no.2 is mother in law of the complainant.
It is further submitted that complainant has made general allegations against the petitioner no.2 in typical fashion to enrope said petitioner in the offence.
It is further submitted that FIR even if taken on its face value, it could not establish offence of section 498(A) and 506 of IPC.

Reading questioned FIR, learned advocate for the applicant submits that right to file FIR has been misused by complainant and it is filed to pressurize the petitioner and therefore, it is submitted to allow the petition.

8. Learned advocate for respondent no.2 opposing plea to quash the FIR would submit that according to FIR, the petitioners were inciting husband of the complainant and it was root cause for offence alleged against the husband.
In view of that, it is submitted that let trial to conduct against the petitioners to test veracity of the allegations.
On this grounds, it is submitted to dismiss the petition.
9. Learned APP for respondent - State adopted the arguments of learned advocate for respondent no.2 - complainant.

sentences.text: 10. Apt to note that allegations levelled in the FIR are general and vague in nature.
In order to establish offence under section 498(A) of IPC, one need to averred that there was harassment or cruelty.

Cruelty means conduct likely to commit suicide or cause grave injury or danger to her life,
limb or health physically or mentally to the complainant or harassment with a view to coercing her or her relatives to meet unlawful demands for property or valuable security.
11. In the present case, FIR even if taken on its face value, so far as petitioner no.2 is concerned, role of the petitioner no.2 is found to be limited of inciting husband of the complainant.
It is alleged that due to such incitement, husband of the complainant was extending physical and mental cruelty to the complainant.
However, specific incidents are missing in the matter.
Causal reference of the petitioners in the FIR is insufficient to take cognizance.

12. Recently, Hon'ble Apex Court warned against misuse of law, while quashing offences under Section 498(A) of Code of Criminal Procedure against Husband and in laws, in case of Ghanshyam Soni versus State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) and Others of 2025 Live Law (SC) 676, observed and held as under:
"10.

entities.text: Ghanshyam Soni versus State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi) and Others of 2025 Live Law (SC) 676
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the FIR shows that the allegations made by the complainant are that in the year 1999, the Appellant inflicted mental and physical cruelty upon her for bringing insufficient dowry.
The Complainant refers to few instances of such atrocities, however the allegations are generic, and rather NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9611/2018 ORDER DATED: 26/09/2025 undefined ambiguous.

The allegations against the family members, who have been unfortunately roped in, is that they used to instigate the Appellant husband to harass the Complainant wife,
and taunted the Complainant for not bringing enough dowry; however, there is no specific incident of harassment or any evidence to that effect.

Similarly, the allegations against the five out of six sisters that they used to insult the Complainant and demanded dowry articles from her, and upon failure beat her up, but there is not even a cursory mention of the incident.
An allegation has also been made against a tailor named Bhagwat that he being a friend of the Appellant instigated him against the Complainant, and was allegedly instrumental in blowing his greed.
Such allegations are merely accusatory and contentious in nature, and do not elaborate a concrete picture of what may have transpired.
For this reason alone, and that the evidence on record is clearly inconsistent with the accusations, the version of the Complainant seems implausible and unreliable.

The following observation in K.
Subba Rao v. State of Telangana Represented by Its Secretary, Department of Home & Ors.2, fits perfectly to the present scenario:
"6. The Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

Subba Rao v. State of Telangana

sentences.text:
The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out."

sentences.text: As regards the Appellant, the purportedly specific allegations levelled against him are also obscure in nature.

Even if the allegations and the case of the prosecution is taken at its face value,
apart from the bald allegations without any specifics of time, date or place, there is no incriminating material found by the prosecution or rather produced by the complainant to NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9611/2018 ORDER DATED: 26/09/2025 undefined substantiate the ingredients of "cruelty" under section 498A IPC, as recently observed in the case of Jaydedeepsinh Pravinsinh Chavda & Ors. v. State of Gujarat and Rajesh Chaddha v. State of Uttar Pradesh.

entities.text: Jaydedeepsinh Pravinsinh Chavda & Ors. v. State of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Rajesh Chaddha v. State of Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Complainant has admittedly failed to produce any medical records or injury reports, x-ray reports, or any witnesses to substantiate her allegations.

We cannot ignore the fact that the Complainant even withdrew her second Complaint dt.
06.12.1999 six days later on 12.12.1999.

There is also no evidence to substantiate the purported demand for dowry allegedly made by the Appellant or his family and the investigative agencies in their own prudence have not added sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 to the chargesheet.

13. It is rather unfortunate that the Complainant being an officer of the State has initiated criminal machinery in such a manner, where the aged parents-in-law, five sisters and one tailor have been arrayed as an accused.
Notwithstanding the possibility of truth behind the allegations of cruelty, this growing tendency to misuse legal provisions has time and again been condemned by this Court.

The observations in Dara Lakshmi Narayana & Ors. v. State of Telangana & Anr., Preeti Gupta & Anr. v. State of Jharkhand &
Anr. aptly captures this concern."
13.

sentences.text: Coming back to the present case, except bald allegations against the petitioner no.2, who is mother in law of the complainant, no specific incident or overtact is alleged against the petitioners.
FIR is found to be abuse of process of law against the petitioner no.2 and allowing the petitioner no.2 to face trial would be absurd process.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/9611/2018 ORDER DATED: 26/09/2025 undefined 14.
In the result, the petition is partly allowed.

The impugned FIR being C.R.No.I - 35 of 2017 registered with Mahila Police Station, Jamnagar as well as all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof are hereby quashed and set aside qua the petitioner no.2 - Ahalyadevi @ Umabaa Chandravijay Singh only.
Rule is made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.

15. Registry to send copy of this order to learned JMFC, Dr.Amdedkar Nagar, Indore, Madhya Pradesh.
